x: The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; Sindhi came in 1967, so only 'Nepali and Konkani' is right.

x: The languages added in 2003 (92nd Amendment) were Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali; Bhojpuri was never in the list.

s: Under which one of the following Constitution Amendment Acts were four languages added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India, thereby raising their number to 22?
x: The 92nd Amendment Act, 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali, raising the number to 22.

s:
The Constitution (71 st Amendment) Act, 1992, amends the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution to include which of the following languages?
1. Konkani
2. Manipuri
3. Nepali
4. Maithili
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; Maithili came with the 92nd Amendment in 2003.

s: Which of the following language is not included in 8th schedule?
x: Rajasthani is not among the 22 scheduled languages; Gujarati and Kashmiri date from 1950 and Dogri from 2003.

s: Which among the following language was added in 8th Schedule of the Indian Constitution in 2003?
x: Santhali was added in 2003 (92nd Amendment) with Bodo, Dogri and Maithili; Konkani and Manipuri came in 1992 and Sindhi in 1967.

s: Which three languages have been added to the 8th Schedule of Indian Constitution by 71st Amendment?
x: The 71st Amendment (1992) added Nepali, Konkani and Manipuri; Sindhi came in 1967, and Kashmiri and Assamese were original entries.

s: From the following languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution pick out the one which is official language of a state
x:
SSC key and most books: Urdu (J&K). Nepali is also an official language of Sikkim, so the stem strictly fits two options (general knowledge, not checked).
Urdu was the official language of the former State of Jammu and Kashmir and is a second official language in several States, so it is the expected answer.

s: Under which one of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts, four languages were added to the languages under the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, there by raising their number to 22?
x: The 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali, taking the Eighth Schedule from 18 to 22 languages.

s: Which one of the following is correct about the languages mentioned in the Constitution of India?
o: State can compel the linguistic minorities to choose their mother tongue as a medium of instruction in primary schools.
‘Angika’ is now included in the 8th Schedule of the Constitution.
Hindi is a national language of India.
Bodo is recognised as language in the 8th Schedule of the Constitution.
x: Bodo was added to the Eighth Schedule in 2003. Angika is not listed, Hindi is the official (not national) language, and Art. 350A only asks States to provide mother-tongue teaching.

s: Which language is not included in 8th schedule of Indian Constitution?
x: Bhojpuri is not in the Eighth Schedule, whereas Urdu, Nepali and Konkani are.

s: How many languages are officially recognised by the Indian Constitution?
x: The Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages since the 92nd Amendment (2003).

s: How many regional languages are recognised by the constitution of India?
x: The Constitution's Eighth Schedule recognises 22 languages.

s: Number of languages recognised by Indian constitution
x: 22 languages are in the Eighth Schedule.

s: Identify the incorrect statement on the linguistic diversity of India:
o: In 1961 census, 1652 languages were listed as mother tongues in India
Kachchi and Sindhi are Indo-European languages
Austric languages are spoken by the tribal groups in Jharkhand
x: Dardi (Dardic) is an Indo-Aryan (Indo-European) language of Jammu and Kashmir, not Sino-Tibetan. The other three statements are true: 1,652 mother tongues in 1961, Kachchhi and Sindhi are Indo-Aryan, and Austric languages are spoken by Jharkhand's tribes.

s: Main language of Dravidians?
x: Telugu is a Dravidian language (with Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam); Marathi and Gujarati are Indo-Aryan and Bodo is Sino-Tibetan.

s: Which one of the following languages belongs to the Austric group?
x: Khasi of Meghalaya belongs to the Mon-Khmer branch of the Austric (Austro-Asiatic) family; Marathi is Indo-Aryan, Ladakhi Sino-Tibetan and Tamil Dravidian.

s: With reference to India, the terms 'Halbi, Ho and Kui' pertain to
x: Halbi (Bastar, Indo-Aryan), Ho (Munda, Jharkhand-Odisha) and Kui (Dravidian, Kondhs of Odisha) are tribal languages, not dance forms, instruments or paintings.

s: Which one of the following languages belongs to the Austric group?
x: Khasi is an Austric (Austro-Asiatic, Mon-Khmer) language; Austric also includes Santhali, Mundari and Bhumij.

s: Which one of the following is the largest linguistic group of India?
x: Indo-Aryan is India's largest language group – about 73% of speakers in older data and 78% in Census 2011 – ahead of Dravidian (about 20%).

s: The Munda language group belongs to which family?
x: The Munda languages (Santhali, Mundari, Ho, Savara) form a branch of the Austric (Austro-Asiatic) family.

s: Which of the following is not the language of Bastar region?
x: Gondi, Halbi and Bhatri are languages of the Bastar region; Sadri (Sadani) is the link language of the Chota Nagpur plateau (Jharkhand, north Chhattisgarh), not Bastar.

s: The speakers of major Indian languages belong to how many language families?
x:
Most books and keys: four families. NextGen Indian Geography 15 p.18 also lists six broad groups (Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Sino-Tibetan, Negroid, Austric and Others).
Indian languages belong to four main families: Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic and Sino-Tibetan.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
s: Vishwa Hindi Diwas is celebrated every year on ____ in order to promote the language world-wide.
x: Vishwa (World) Hindi Diwas is observed on 10 January, the date of the first World Hindi Conference (Nagpur, 1975); Hindi Diwas is 14 September.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that it shall be the endeavour of every State to provide adequate facility for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education?
x: Article 350A asks every State and local authority to provide instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for linguistic-minority children.

s: Which Article of Indian Constitution provides the procedure for adoption of official Language or Languages of the State?
x: Article 345 lets a State Legislature adopt one or more languages as the State's official language; 343 is the Union language, 344 the Commission, 346 inter-State communication.

s: Under Article 344 of Indian Constitution, the first ‘Official language Commission’ was established
o: in 1950, under the Chairmanship of KM Munshi.
in 1955, under the Chairmanship of BG Kher.
in 1960, Under the Chairmanship of MC Chagala.
in 1965, under the Chairmanship of Humayun Kabir.
x: Under Article 344 the President appointed the Official Language Commission in 1955 under B.G. Kher; it reported in 1956.

s: Official Language Commission was ended in …………
x:
Printed key: 1976. Strictly the only Official Language Commission (B.G. Kher, 1955) ended with its report in 1956, a date not offered (Laxmikanth ch.74).
The printed key 1976 is the year the Committee of Parliament on Official Language was set up under the Official Languages Act, 1963, and of the Official Language Rules. No second Official Language Commission was appointed after Kher's.

s:
Which of the following is/are not central feature of Article 343 of the Constitution of India?

I. Hindi in Devanagiri script shall be the National language of the Union.

II. The official language of the union shall be Hindi in Devanagiri script.

III. English language shall continue to be used for official purpose within states.

IV. If two or more states agree, Hindi language should be the official language of communication between the states.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Article 343 makes Hindi in Devanagari the official language of the Union, not a 'national language'; English within States and Hindi between States by agreement are not in Art. 343 (the latter is Art. 346). So I, III and IV are not its features.

s: The Government of India appointed the Official Language Commission in 1955. Who was the Chairman of the Commission?
x: B.G. Kher, former Chief Minister of Bombay, chaired the Official Language Commission set up in 1955. Fazl Ali headed the States Reorganisation Commission.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017

x: The Constitution gives national-language status to no language; Hindi in Devanagari is only the official language of the Union.

s: The language spoken by the largest number of people in the world is :

Most books and keys: Mandarin (native speakers). Counting second-language users too, Ethnologue puts English first (general knowledge, not checked).
Mandarin Chinese has the largest number of native speakers in the world and is the standard answer; Hindi and English come after it on that count.

s: Which Indian language, is spoken the most in the world after Hindi?
x: After Hindi, Bengali is the most spoken Indian language in the world (7th worldwide); Telugu and Tamil rank lower.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
s: Which of the following states in India has brought out a comprehensive bilingual tribal dictionary seen as a measure to preserve vanishing native languages in the state?
x: Odisha published a comprehensive bilingual tribal dictionary series to preserve its vanishing tribal languages.

s: Movement of people from a village to a small town and later to a city is known as
x: Step-wise migration is movement in stages – village to small town, then to a larger town or city (Ravenstein's migration by stages).

s: Among the following whose name is associated with migration theory?
x: Everett S. Lee gave the push-pull 'A Theory of Migration' (1966); Notestein and Thompson are linked with demographic transition and Doubleday with the diet theory.

s: The dominant trend of migrant labour is
x: Most migrant labour in India is seasonal or circular, moving for work in the lean farm season and returning home.

s: Which one of the following is the biggest cause of incidence of migration of female persons in India?
x: Marriage is the main reason women migrate: PLFS 2020-21 shows 86.8% of female migrants moved for marriage, while men move mainly for employment.

s: According to the Census 2011, in India, what is the percentage of people (approximately) considered to be migrants (internal) i.e. now settled in a place different from their previous residence?
x: Census 2011 counted 455.8 million migrants by last residence, about 37.6% of the population, so 35% is the nearest option.

s: During the last 30 years Delhi has received the highest number of migrants from :
x: Uttar Pradesh is the largest source of migrants to Delhi, followed by Bihar; Haryana and Punjab send far fewer.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Recently, all the countries of the United Nations have adopted the first-ever compact for international migration, the 'Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM)'.
2. The objectives and commitments stated in the GCM are binding on the UN member countries.
3. The GCM addresses internal migration or internally displaced people also in its objectives and commitments.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: All three are wrong: the GCM (Marrakech, endorsed by the UNGA on 19 Dec 2018) was not adopted by all members, is non-binding, and covers only international migration.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Recently, all the countries of the United Nations have adopted the first-ever compact for international migration, the ‘Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM)’.
2. The objectives and commitments stated in the GCM are binding on the UN member countries.
3. The GCM addresses internal migration or internally displaced people also in its objectives and commitments.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: None is correct: not all UN members adopted the GCM, it is legally non-binding, and it addresses international, not internal, migration.

src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I Mains General Studies & Mental Abilit

s: Sir Edwin Lutyens was the architect of which city?
x: Sir Edwin Lutyens (with Herbert Baker) designed New Delhi, the imperial capital; Chandigarh was planned by Le Corbusier (official key: Chandigarh).

s: Sir Edwin Lutyens was the architect of the city of
x: Sir Edwin Lutyens was the chief architect of New Delhi; Chandigarh was the work of Le Corbusier (official key: Chandigarh).

s: Which of the following is not a planned capital city?
x: Chandigarh, Bhubaneswar and Gandhinagar are planned post-1947 capitals; Bengaluru grew unplanned.

s:
Which of the following statements about town planning in British India in early 19th century is/are correct?

I. The funds for town improvement were also raised through public lotteries.

II. The threats of epidemics gave an impetus to town planning in the early decades of 19th century.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Both are true: epidemic fears pushed early 19th-century town planning, and town improvement in Calcutta was funded partly through public lotteries (Lottery Committee).

s: Which of the following is not a twin city of India?
x: Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar, Hubli-Dharwad and Cuttack-Bhubaneswar are twin cities; Thrissur and Thiruvalla are not a pair.

s: Which of the urban studies perspectives refers to concentric zones of modern urban development?
x:
Printed key: geographical perspective. Burgess's concentric zones come from the Chicago School's human-ecology approach, which none of the options names exactly.
The printed key treats the concentric-zone model of urban growth (E.W. Burgess) as the geographical (spatial) perspective of urban studies.

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: Which city of India has the highest population in 2017 (excluding urban agglomeration)?
x: Mumbai (Greater Mumbai) is India's most populous city proper, ahead of Delhi, Bengaluru and Kolkata.

s:
Arrange the following cities in decreasing order of population:
A. Bangalore
B. Ahmedabad
C. Kanpur
D. Delhi
E. Kolkata

s: Find the correct arrangement of the following urban agglomerations in descending order as per their population size according to Census 2011.

x:
Most keys: 6th (urban agglomeration ranking). As a city proper (GHMC, about 68 lakh) Hyderabad ranked 4th after Mumbai, Delhi and Bengaluru (general knowledge, not checked).
As an urban agglomeration Hyderabad (77.5 lakh) ranked 6th in Census 2011 after Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Bengaluru.

s: According to 2011 census, the most populous Indian city
x: Greater Mumbai was the most populous city in Census 2011 (about 1.24 crore; UA 1.84 crore), ahead of Delhi and Kolkata.

s: As per 2011 Census, the most populous city in India is
x: In Census 2011 Greater Mumbai was the most populous city (UA about 1.84 crore), ahead of Delhi and Kolkata.

s: This is the most urbanised state in India as per 2011 census
x: Goa (62.17%) was the most urbanised State in Census 2011.

s: Which State in India has the largest number of towns ?
x: Tamil Nadu has the most towns: 832 in Census 2001 (Uttar Pradesh 704) and 1,097 in 2011 (UP about 915). The official key gave Uttar Pradesh, which is second (official key: Uttar Pradesh).

s: In 2011 census which one among the following states has not registered the highest growth in urban population
x: Sikkim and Kerala led India's urban growth in 2001-11 (census-town reclassification); Goa, already the most urbanised State, grew only about 35% – the slowest of the four – so it is the key.

s: Which one of the following is the correct ascending sequence of states with regard to percentage of Urban population (2011)?
x: Census 2011 urban shares: Maharashtra 45.2% < Kerala 47.7% < Mizoram 52.1% < Goa 62.2%.

s: Which is the cause of growing urbanisation in India ?
o: Growth of industry and trade in the urban areas
Excessive pressure of population in rural areas
x: Urbanisation is driven by industry and trade in towns (pull) and by rural population pressure and low farm productivity (push), so all of the above.

s: The most important reason for higher absolute increase in urban population in India compared to rural population in the decade from 2001 to 2011 could be due to
o: migration from rural to urban areas
higher death rate in rural areas due to lesser access to medical facilities
better methods of birth control in rural areas
categorization of erstwhile rural areas as urban areas
x: Between 2001 and 2011 census towns rose from 1,362 to 3,894; reclassification of rural areas as urban explains more of the urban jump than migration.

x:

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. In any nation, human development outcomes are a function of economic growth, social policy and poverty reduction measures at the macro-level.

II. The expansion of human development in terms of health and education attainment, reduction of income poverty and economic growth is linked in a synergistic manner.

III. Investment in health and education can enhance human functioning which can eventually alleviate income poverty by improving employability.

IV. Resources generated through income, poverty reduction and economic growth can be used to enhance human development.
Which of the statements given above are logical and correct?
x: Human development, growth and poverty reduction reinforce each other both ways, so all four statements I, II, III and IV are logical and correct.

s: In the context of any country, which one of the following would be considered as part of its social capital?
o: The proportion of literates in the population.
The stock of its buildings, other infrastructure and machines.
The size of population in the working age group.
The level of mutual trust and harmony in the society.
x: Social capital is the trust, harmony and networks in a society; literacy is human capital and buildings or machines are physical capital.
